key_insight: MF-Diffuser makes offline multi-agent diffusion planning scalable by modeling many-agent behavior in mean-field trajectory-distribution space instead of the full joint trajectory space.
engineering_relevance: This enables offline training and deployment of large-scale coordination policies for systems with thousands of agents while retaining theoretical guarantees on approximation error and equilibrium quality.
method: Lift trajectory planning to Wasserstein space over trajectory distributions.
Use a value-weighted chaotic entropy objective to balance return maximization and generative fidelity.
Apply a hierarchical coarse-to-fine denoising scheme that gradually expands the agent population.
evidence_signal: Across three mean-field RL benchmarks covering stage games, sequential dynamics, and adversarial team competition, the method achieves the best return in most settings, especially with suboptimal offline data and at scales of N >= 10^3.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the mean-field approximation and offline data coverage, so systems with weak representative-agent structure or severe distribution mismatch may be harder to scale reliably.
paper_title: Mean-Field Diffuser: Scaling Offline MARL to Thousands of Agents
